A few words to know

competence
An officially assigned area of power or responsibility.
attribution
Connecting a mark or act to a particular person.
conditional
Only applying when a stated condition is met.
discrepancy
A difference between records or results.
beneficiary
Someone intended to receive a benefit.
corroborate
To support a claim using independent evidence.

04 · Read & review

The transcript

Submit all six answers to unlock the transcript. You can then listen and read together.

When Fiona Bell confirmed that the trust's records team had inspected the sheet headed 'Delegated authority — September 2011', Emma expected her investigation to move from institutional procedure towards named decision-makers. The document delivered a more limited, though genuinely useful, distinction.

It assigned responsibilities among a scheme administrator, finance manager and trust chair. A member of staff could initiate a request for exceptional treatment; another role could authorise that departure from ordinary procedure. The sheet described competences attached to offices. It was not an authorisation register and did not identify the approver of any individual transaction.

Two faint sets of initials appeared beside the descriptions, Fiona reported. Their interpretation remained uncertain: the marks could signify initials, an internal check or something else. Neither Emma nor the records team had a reliable basis for attributing them to a named person. Emma declined to convert imperfect legibility into a speculative allegation.

Sarah nevertheless raised Malcolm Vale. As chair of the Glenarraidh Education Trust, he might have possessed the higher level of delegated authority described by the document. Emma accepted the possibility and rejected the inference. Possessing authority is not evidence of exercising it; still less does it establish a payment, an improper decision or a motive connected with Claire Morrison's disappearance.

A paragraph on the sheet required exceptions above a specified financial threshold to be referred to the chair. The amount was unreadable on the copy currently available. Fiona also lacked a reliable count of cases, let alone evidence identifying any exception above the threshold. The referral rule therefore remained conditional. Emma could not claim it had actually been triggered.

The resemblance between this administrative trail and the anonymous caller's warning about payment approvals was striking. Yet a caller whose identity and sources were unverified could not authenticate the newly inspected guidance. The same caution applied to Helen Ward's redacted copy of her cousin's selection notice. It described a conditional award but demonstrated neither authorisation nor transfer. Helen's family had declined further banking disclosure, a boundary Emma would respect.

Emma formulated a narrower request. Could the team obtain a legible reproduction of the threshold, establish what sort of marks appeared by the office titles and report whether the surviving exceptions could be counted without identifying students? Each task concerned the quality and structure of evidence rather than the exposure of a private beneficiary.

Sarah created a diagram with four successive claims: Requested, Authorised, Transferred, Received. The first two appeared in the trust's procedural language. Transaction records would be needed for the third, and reliable evidence of arrival for the fourth. A discrepancy between stages could have routine explanations; its mere existence would not prove misconduct.

Fiona's final message supplied another archival lead. A storage inventory mentioned an 'authorisation register', but no one had yet found the register. Its condition, scope and very survival were uncertain. Emma added the reference to her notes without calling it recovered evidence.

In the silence of her office, the distinction became clear. The delegated-authority sheet could tell her who was entitled to approve an exceptional request. A completed authorisation entry might tell her who actually approved one. Only subsequent records could establish whether money moved.

She underlined the unresolved question: Where is the record of decisions made under this authority?
